newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady, strong mogas balances Iraq.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady, strong mogas balances Iraq.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended steady on Wednesday as fears of a flood of Iraqi exports next month were tempered by prompt tightness in the U.S. gasoline market.
August Brent, which went off the board at the close of trade, ended one cent higher at $18.40 a barrel. August gas oil earlier closed up $1.00 at $163.75 a tonne.
"I don't think anyone was willing to sell heavily when there's still so much uncertainty over Iraq and U.S. gasoline is clearly pretty tight," said one broker.

Data from the U.S. Department of Energy indicated a 3.9 million barrel draw on gasoline stocks last week. And production is set to be cut back soon as one of the country's largest gasoline producing plants, Tosco's Bayway refinery, is scheduled to close for several weeks in late July for maintenance.
"The market sentiment is for crude to go lower, but prompt gasoline in the States is pretty tight and at the front end gasoline cracks have widened out a lot recently," said one dealer.
Strength at the front end of the market helped to push the front Brent spread out of contango ahead of the expiry, brokers said. August/September ended 11 cents in backwardation.
But bearish news about Iraqi oil exports ensured that crude futures did not track gasoline higher.

Traders are bracing themselves for Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal to reach 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) in August, with virtually all of this quarter's $1-billion of sales concentrated in that month.

Western diplomats at the United Nations said on Tuesday that Iraq would be allowed to carry over only five percent of its sales in the current 90 day sales period, which started on June 8, to the next quarter.
This would mean Iraq, having delayed the restart of exports for two months, will have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August than previously expected, or forego some of its sales.
"At the moment the North Sea crude looks fairly stable but there is a feeling that with Iraq pumping quite a bit and come September the market will be well-supplied," said one.
Exports in the first six-month term of the scheme averaged around 660,000 bpd.
